name: The Liberty
insider_take: This isn't just a hotel—it's a piece of Boston history where revolutionaries once plotted and luxury now reigns.
whats_special: The Liberty occupies the former Suffolk County Jail (1851), where Boston Strangler Albert DeSalvo was once held. The stunning transformation preserves original details like stone archways and wrought-iron catwalks, now serving as dramatic design elements. Your "cell" might feature 14-foot ceilings and river views—quite the upgrade from its correctional past.
pro_tip: Book a Liberty Suite to sleep in what was once the jail's drunk tank—now featuring Italian marble bathrooms and city skyline views. The contrast is deliciously ironic.
dont_miss: The hotel's restaurant Clink is named after the building's jailhouse slang, and the fitness center occupies former jail cells. Walk the Freedom Trail starting just blocks away, or catch a Red Sox game at nearby Fenway Park—both quintessentially Boston experiences within easy reach.
pros: Historic charm in converted 19th-century jail building
Prime location in Boston's Beacon Hill neighborhood
Part of prestigious Marriott STARS Program with exclusive benefits
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes
Premium pricing typical of luxury Boston hotels
